introduction.text: The Berretta del Prete is a Roman mausoleum located in the Parco regionale dell'Appia antica near Santa Maria delle Mole, notable for its dome, height over 12 m, and its historical significance as a funerary monument dating to the late Roman period.

history.description: A brick tomb of the "a edicola" type adjacent to the mausoleum, datable to the 2nd century.
Construction of the mausoleum, a dome structure with semicircular niches, dated to the years near 300.
Document of 950 records the purchase of the mausoleum and surrounding land by the church of San Gregorio al Celio, which retained ownership until 1828.
In 1981, exploratory excavations led by archaeologist Marisa de Spagnolis uncovered marble fragments, including a column with an ibis and serpent, now housed in the Museo Nazionale Romano.

design.description: The mausoleum features a dome exceeding 12 m in height, external semicircular niches, and a single entrance door with a peperino lintel less than one meter wide.

art.description: Marble column with an ibis and serpent motif, recovered during the 1981 excavations, now displayed at the Museo Nazionale Romano.
